title: DC-area forecast: Damp by late evening with showers and storms into tonight
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Other than a small chance of a brief shower or pop-up storm, it's not until after 8 or 9 p.m. that we need to watch a cluster or line of storms more effectively dampen the region into the night. One or two storms could have gusty winds.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Other than a small chance of a brief shower or pop-up storm, it's not until after 8 or 9 p.m. that we need to watch a cluster or line of storms more effectively dampen the region into the night. One or two storms could have gusty winds. Evening 70s slowly sag to lows in the mid-60s to near 70.

What's next? Maybe a leftover shower or two Sunday with decreasing humidity. Mostly sunny and pleasant Monday and Tuesday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Scattered showers and a few thunderstorms move in from the west this evening, mainly after 8 or 9 p.m., and continue into the overnight. Skies are mostly cloudy, with lows ranging from the mid-60s to near 70. Patchy fog possible, with a quarter inch of rain broadly possible outside of any downpours. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Sunday): A leftover shower could be around early Sunday morning before quickly ending. Another pop-up shower is possible mid- to late afternoon as some instability lingers despite clearing skies. Less humid as afternoon highs reach near 80 to mid-80s. Winds from the west-northwest turn a bit breezy, with late-day gusts near 20 mph. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Quiet, comfortable, and mostly clear. Overnight lows range from near 60 to the mid-60s while humidity remains a non-issue. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Monday and Tuesday look to offer a dry and pleasant start to the workweek as high pressure builds into the region, bringing a welcome break from the humidity. Highs around 80 to 85 with mostly sunny skies and comfortable dew points in the mid- to upper 50s. Winds from the northeast remain light, around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

More typical August warmth and humidity returns Wednesday as a dip in the jet stream over the Great Lakes tracks east. With a breeze more from the south, highs climb into the mid- to upper 80s with increasing humidity (dew points rising into the low to mid-60s). A shower or storm chance could return by afternoon or evening. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: A muggy Saturday with showers early, but maybe some dry time during the afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 22

The powerful 1933 Chesapeake-Potomac hurricane slammed into Hampton Roads with near-100 mph winds and an 8-foot storm surge, devastating coastal Virginia before tracking north toward the DC region.
